newsitem.title: Philippines: Philippine stocks end higher in see-saw trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine stocks end higher in see-saw trade.

text.p: * Index seen heading for record high of 3,375.94 pts
Manila stocks bounced into positive territory at the close on Tuesday as investors bought blue chips and secondliners after a soft opening, traders said.
The composite index ended 18.89 points higher at 3,341.99 points, but off the day's high of 3,346.76.
"Trading heightened at midsession as investors grabbed blue chips after a sluggish opening. Then, they cashed-in some gains at close," said Juanis Barredo, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.

Traders said reports that Moody's Investor Service plans to upgrade the credit rating of 11 Philippine banks perked up sentiment. They attributed the sluggish start to the 35-point drop in the Dow Jones index overnight.
Buying on blue-chips San Miguel Corp, Manila Electric Co, Philippine National Bank and secondliners Fil-Estate, Belle Resources and SM Prime pushed up the index, traders said.
"I expect the index to test its all time high of 3,375.94 points in the next (few) sessions," said Barredo.
